statements.claim: For seven days Indra poured thunder, wind and water over Vrindavan because the cowherds, at a boy's urging, had turned their worship away from him and toward a hill.
statements.evidence: Storm and its cause are the established preceding event in the arc (prev story DKS_0087); SB 10.27.11 has Indra say 'by me this cowherd home was about to be destroyed by wind and rain', and the Harivamsha passage in the adjacent pack (1.74) gives 'excessive rain extending over seven nights'.

statements.claim: Indra came down quietly, alone, approaching in seclusion, ashamed, his offense heavy on him.
statements.evidence: SB 10.27.1: 'vivikta upasaṅgamya vrīḍītaḥ kṛta-helanaḥ' — approached in seclusion, ashamed, having committed an offense.

statements.claim: He had seen and heard enough of Krishna's boundless power to know who stood before him.
statements.evidence: SB 10.27.2: 'dṛṣṭa-śrutānubhāvo 'sya kṛṣṇasyāmita-tejasaḥ' — having seen and heard of Krishna's boundless power.

statements.claim: Indra touched Krishna's feet with his crown.
statements.evidence: Pack excerpt: 'Indra, ashamed, approached Krishna in seclusion, touched his feet with his crown' (rendered from verses 1-15).

statements.claim: "I was drunk on my own lordship... I did not know your power, and so I offended you. Forgive me, Lord. Let such a wish never rise in me again."
statements.evidence: Pack excerpt: 'I, intoxicated by my sovereignty, have offended you, not knowing your power; forgive me, Lord, and may such evil intention never arise in me again.'

statements.claim: A man intoxicated with rule and riches cannot see the hand that holds the rod of chastisement.
statements.evidence: SB 10.27.15: 'mām aiśvarya-śrī-madāndho daṇḍa-pāṇiṃ na paśyati'.

statements.claim: He named Krishna the father and teacher of all the worlds, the lord before whom all must bow, with time holding its punishment ready.
statements.evidence: SB 10.27.5: 'pitā gurus tvaṃ jagatām adhīśo duratyayaḥ kāla upātta-daṇḍaḥ'.

statements.claim: Krishna had come down to lighten the burden of the earth, a burden the gods could not lay down.
statements.evidence: SB 10.27.8: 'tavāvatāro 'yam adhokṣajeha bhuvo bharāṇām uru-bhāra-janmanām' — this descent to lighten the earth's heavy burden.

statements.claim: "By me this home of the cowherds was about to be destroyed by wind and rain. And by you I have been spared. My arrogance is broken. My effort has come to nothing."
statements.evidence: SB 10.27.11-12: 'mayedaṃ bhagavan goṣṭha-nāśāyāsāra-vāyubhiḥ / tvayeśānugṛhīto 'smi dhvasta-stambho vṛthodyamaḥ'.

statements.claim: Krishna replied, "Go, Shakra. May all be well with you. Do what I ask of you."
statements.evidence: SB 10.27.16: 'gamyatāṃ śakra bhadraṃ vaḥ kriyatāṃ me 'nuśāsanam'.

statements.claim: The forest was quiet after the rain, leaves wet and ground soft, with no witness to the meeting.
statements.evidence: Atmospheric setting consistent with Indra approaching in seclusion (10.27.1); no sourceable fact asserted.

notes: All claims map directly to SB 10.27.1-16 or the established preceding storm narrative; no unsupported or contradicted claims.

statements.claim: Surabhi, the divine cow, stepped forward to praise Krishna.
statements.evidence: SB 10.27.17-18: 'athāha surabhiḥ kṛṣṇam abhivandya manasvinī' — Surabhi, wise, bowed to and addressed Krishna.

statements.claim: Surabhi is the mother of all the cattle of heaven and earth.
statements.evidence: Traditional epithet of Surabhi (the divine cow per pack); the pack itself calls her 'the divine cow' — epithet, not a sourceable event in the pack.

statements.claim: "You are our highest deity... You are our very Indra, lord of the world. Urged by Brahma, we shall now consecrate you as Indra."
statements.evidence: SB 10.27.19-20: 'tvaṃ naḥ paramakaṃ daivaṃ tvaṃ na indro jagat-pate / indraṃ nas tvābhiṣekṣyāmo brahmaṇā coditā vayam'.

statements.claim: Indra was urged on by Surabhi and the divine mothers, and came with the sages of the gods, Tumburu, Narada, Gandharvas, Vidyadharas, Siddhas and Charanas.
statements.evidence: SB 10.27.22-23: 'indraḥ surarṣibhiḥ sākaṃ codito deva-mātṛbhiḥ / tatrāgatās tumburu-nāradādayo gandharva-vidyādhara-siddha-cāraṇāḥ'.

statements.claim: Indra brought the water of the celestial Ganga and bathed Krishna with it, giving him the name Govinda.
statements.evidence: Pack excerpt: 'Indra, with the waters of the celestial Ganga, bathed Krishna and named him Govinda' (10.27.20-22); SB 10.27.27: 'iti go-gokula-patiṃ govindam abhiṣicya saḥ'.

statements.claim: "The people of this world will sing of you as Govinda," spoken in the words of the older account.
statements.evidence: Harivamsha 1.74: 'the people of this world will hymn thee as Govinda'; Vishnu Purana 5.12: 'as the Indra of the cows, thou shalt be called Govinda'.

statements.claim: The assembled gods praised Krishna and showered him with wonderful flowers from the sky.
statements.evidence: SB 10.27.24: 'taṃ tuṣṭuvur deva-nikāya-ketavo hy avākiraṃś cādbhuta-puṣpa-vṛṣṭibhiḥ'.

statements.claim: When Krishna was consecrated, the rivers ran with many kinds of sweetness and the trees oozed honey.
statements.evidence: SB 10.27.25: 'nānā-rasaughāḥ sarito vṛkṣā āsan madhu-sravāḥ'.

statements.claim: The name Govinda — lord of the cows and cowherds — stuck and never left him.
statements.evidence: SB 10.27.27 ('go-gokula-patiṃ govindam'); Vishnu Purana 5.12 ('Indra of the cows... called Govinda'); closing reflection is commentary, not a factual assertion.

notes: Clean; ceremony details (celestial Ganga, Govinda naming, flower showers, honey-dripping trees) all in SB 10.27.17-27 / Harivamsha 1.74 / VP 5.12.

statements.claim: Krishna's flute song awakened remembrance of him in the gopis, and they began to describe him to one another.
statements.evidence: SB 10.21.2-3: 'veṇu-gītaṃ smarodayam... tad varṇayitum ārabdhāḥ smarantyaḥ kṛṣṇa-ceṣṭitam'.

statements.claim: He wore a peacock feather, golden-yellow cloth, and a garland of forest flowers, and filled the flute with the nectar of his lips, with cowherd boys around him.
statements.evidence: SB 10.21.4: 'barhāpīḍaṃ... vāsaḥ kanaka-kapiśaṃ vaijayantīṃ ca mālām... adhara-sudhayāpūrayan... gopa-vṛndair'.

statements.claim: His music was pleasing to every living thing.
statements.evidence: SB 10.21.5: 'veṇu-ravaṃ rājan sarva-bhūta-manoharam'.

statements.claim: Even the dull-witted deer stopped to listen and worshipped him with looks of love.
statements.evidence: SB 10.21.10: 'dhanyāḥ sma mūḍha-gatayo 'pi hariṇya etā... pūjāṃ dadhur viracitāṃ praṇayāvalokaiḥ'.

statements.claim: The women of heaven in their flying chariots went still, flowers falling loose from their hair.
statements.evidence: SB 10.21.11: 'devyo vimāna-gatayaḥ smara-nunna-sārā bhraśyat-prasūna-kabarā mumuhur vinīvyaḥ'.

statements.claim: The cows drank the music with lifted ears, and calves with milk still on their mouths stood motionless with tears in their eyes, holding Govinda in their hearts.
statements.evidence: SB 10.21.12: 'gāvaś ca... pīyūṣam uttabhita-karṇa-puṭaiḥ pibantyaḥ / śāvāḥ snuta-stana-payaḥ-kavalāḥ sma tasthur govindam ātmani dṛśāśru-kalāḥ'.

statements.claim: Birds and sages climbed the branches and listened with closed eyes, without a word.
statements.evidence: SB 10.21.13: 'vihagā munayo vane 'smin... āruhya ye druma-bhujān rucira-pravālān śṛṇvanti mīlita-dṛśo vigatānya-vācaḥ'.

statements.claim: The rivers, their current broken, reached out with arms of water to touch his feet, offering lotuses.
statements.evidence: SB 10.21.14: 'nadyas tadā... bhagna-vegāḥ... āliṅgana-sthagitam ūrmi-bhujair murārer gṛhṇanti pāda-yugalaṃ kamalopahārāḥ'.

statements.claim: A single cloud stayed over Krishna and his friends like an umbrella as they walked the herds in the heat of the day.
statements.evidence: SB 10.21.15: 'dṛṣṭvātape vraja-paśūn saha rāma-gopaiḥ... vyadhāt sva-vapuṣāmbuda ātapatram' — a cloud made an umbrella of its body; verse places the walk in the heat with Rāma and the cowherds.

statements.claim: Govardhana is the greatest of his servants because his feet touched it and it feeds him and his cattle with water, grass and roots.
statements.evidence: SB 10.21.17: 'hantāyam adrir abalā hari-dāsa-varyo yad rāma-kṛṣṇa-caraṇa-sparaśa-pramodaḥ... pānīya-sūyavasa-kandara-kandamūlaiḥ'.

notes: Every image (deer, goddesses, cows, calves, birds/sages, rivers, cloud, hill) maps to a specific verse in SB 10.21.1-19.

statements.claim: The young unmarried girls of Vrindavan went down to the Yamuna before dawn and bathed in it.
statements.evidence: SB 10.22.1: 'āplutyāmbhasi kālindyā jalānte codite 'ruṇe' — bathing in the waters of the Kalindi (Yamuna) at the rise of dawn.

statements.claim: The verses call them kumaryas — young girls, not yet married.
statements.evidence: SB 10.22.4: 'evaṃ māsaṃ vrataṃ ceruḥ kumāryaḥ kṛṣṇa-cetasaḥ'.

statements.claim: Through the first month of winter they performed the vow every morning.
statements.evidence: SB 10.22.4 ('for a month they performed the vow'); index summary: 'Through the first month of winter the gopis keep their vow, bathing before dawn in the Yamuna'.

statements.claim: At the water's edge they made an image of the goddess Katyayani and worshipped her with fragrant paste, garlands, offerings, incense and a burning lamp.
statements.evidence: SB 10.22.2: 'gandhair mālyaiḥ surabhibhir balibhir dhūpa-dīpakaiḥ'; pack excerpt: 'worshipping an image of the goddess'.

statements.claim: Their single prayer was: "O Katyayani... make Nanda's son my husband."
statements.evidence: SB 10.22.3 addresses Katyayani as 'mahā-māye mahā-yoginy adhīśvari'; pack excerpt: 'with the single prayer that Nanda's son become their husband'; 10.22.4: 'kṛṣṇa-cetasaḥ' — minds fixed on Krishna.

statements.claim: They rose at dawn and went linked arm in arm with one another.
statements.evidence: SB 10.22.5: 'ūṣasy utthāya gotraiḥ svair anyonyābaddha-bāhavaḥ' — rising at dawn, holding one another's arms.

statements.claim: They asked for nothing else — not riches, long life, or good fortune.
statements.evidence: Consistent with the pack's single-prayer emphasis (10.22.4); negative framing is narrative, not a separately sourceable claim.

statements.claim: Their mothers knew and said nothing.
statements.evidence: Minor narrative texture; not in the pack's verses 1-5 but contradicts nothing.

statements.claim: By the time the sun was fully up they would be dressed and turning for home.
statements.evidence: Atmospheric continuation of the pre-dawn bathing scene; no factual assertion in the pack to verify.

notes: Core vow details all supported by SB 10.22.1-5; remaining items are connective texture.

statements.claim: The girls laid their clothes on the riverbank and entered the water, as before.
statements.evidence: SB 10.22.6: 'nadyāḥ kadācid āgatya tīre nikṣipya pūrva-vat' — coming to the river, placing clothes on the bank as before.

statements.claim: Krishna understood what their discipline was for; the verses call him the master of all masters of yoga.
statements.evidence: SB 10.22.7: 'bhagavāṃs tad abhipretya kṛṣṇo yogeśvareśvaraḥ'.

statements.claim: He gathered up their garments and quickly climbed a kadamba (nīpa) tree.
statements.evidence: SB 10.22.8: 'tāsāṃ vāsāṃsy upādāya nīpam āruhya satvaraḥ'.

statements.claim: Laughing, he called down: come, one by one, and take back what is yours.
statements.evidence: SB 10.22.9: 'atrāgatya... kāmaṃ svaṃ svaṃ vāsaḥ pragṛhyatām'; the jest (kṣvelita) at 10.22.11.

statements.claim: The gopis knew he had never once spoken an untruth to them, and found no cruelty in the jest.
statements.evidence: SB 10.22.10: 'na mayodita-pūrvaṃ vā anṛtaṃ tad ime viduḥ' — they knew he had never uttered an untruth before; 10.22.11 'kṣvelitaṃ' — play/jest.

statements.claim: The gopis were flooded with love, like a lamp flaring when a hand is cupped near it.
statements.evidence: SB 10.22.11: 'tasya tat kṣvelitaṃ dṛṣṭvā gopyaḥ prema-pariplutāḥ' — seeing his jest, the gopis were flooded with love; lamp simile is narrative embellishment of 'flooded with love'.

statements.claim: The kadamba tree stood close to the water, and the girls stood waist-deep in the cold river looking up at him.
statements.evidence: Scene-setting consistent with 10.22.6-11 (clothes on the bank, tree climbed, girls in the water); physical details are atmosphere.

notes: All plot points map directly to SB 10.22.6-11.

statements.claim: The gopis answered from the water, calling him the dear son of Nanda, the dark and beautiful one, saying they were his maidservants and would do whatever he asked.
statements.evidence: SB 10.22.13-14: 'mānayaṃ bhoḥ kṛthās tvāṃ tu nanda-gopa-sutaṃ priyam / śyāmasundara te dāsyaḥ karavāma tavoditam'.

statements.claim: All the girls came out of the water together, trembling with cold, and stood before him.
statements.evidence: SB 10.22.16: 'tato jalāśayāt sarvā dārikāḥ śīta-vepitāḥ'.

statements.claim: Their hands pressed together above their heads as they stood before him.
statements.evidence: Gesture not stated in the pack passage (10.22.16 only says they came out trembling with cold); descriptive detail, contradicts nothing in the pack.

statements.claim: Krishna, pleased by the purity of their hearts, told them that bathing naked while keeping their vow showed disregard for the gods, which had to be answered.
statements.evidence: SB 10.22.17-18: 'śuddha-bhāva-prasāditaḥ... yūyaṃ vivastrā yad apo dhṛta-vratā vyagāhataitat tad u deva-helanam'.

statements.claim: "Your resolve is known to me. This worship of me — I have seen it."
statements.evidence: SB 10.22.24: 'saṅkalpo viditaḥ sādhvyo bhavatīnāṃ mad-arcanam'.

statements.claim: "Go back to Vraja now. The nights you have wished for will come to you."
statements.evidence: SB 10.22.26: 'yātābalā vrajaṃ siddhā mayemā raṃsyathā kṣapāḥ' — go to Vraja, successful; with me you will enjoy these nights.

statements.claim: They felt no resentment and were joyful in the company of their beloved.
statements.evidence: SB 10.22.21-22: 'nābhyasūyan priya-saṅga-nirvṛtāḥ... paridhāya sva-vāsāṃsi preṣṭha-saṅgama-sajjitāḥ'.

notes: All substantive claims (maidservant reply, coming out shivering, deva-helana rebuke, resolve known, nights to come, joy) map to SB 10.22.12-27.

statements.claim: Krishna and Balarama were pasturing cattle not far from home with the cowherd boys, and hunger came over them.
statements.evidence: SB 10.23.6: 'gāś cārayantāv avidūra odanaṃ rāmācyutau vo laṣato bubhukṣitau' — pasturing cows not far away, Rāma and Acyuta, hungry, want cooked rice.

statements.claim: A company of brahmanas, learned and well-versed in the Vedas, had gathered to perform a sacrifice.
statements.evidence: SB 10.23.2: 'prayāta deva-yajanaṃ brāhmaṇā brahma-vādinaḥ' — the brahmanas, speakers of Brahman, went to the sacrificial site; pack excerpt: 'performing the Angirasa sacrifice'.

statements.claim: Krishna sent the boys to them with the request for food in his name.
statements.evidence: SB 10.23.3-4: 'tatra gatvaudanaṃ gopā yācatāsmad-visarjitāḥ / ity ādiṣṭā bhagavatā gatvā yācanta te tathā'.

statements.claim: The boys asked: "O gods of the earth, listen to us: we come at Krishna's bidding. While pasturing the cows not far from here, Balarama and Krishna have grown hungry, and they ask for food."
statements.evidence: SB 10.23.5-6: 'he bhūmi-devāḥ śṛṇuta kṛṣṇasyādeśa-kāriṇaḥ / gāś cārayantāv avidūra odanaṃ rāmācyutau vo laṣato bubhukṣitau'.

statements.claim: The brahmanas neither said yes nor no; they simply did not heed the request.
statements.evidence: SB 10.23.8: 'iti te bhagavad-yācñāṃ śṛṇvanto 'pi na śuśruvuḥ'; 10.23.11: 'na te yad om iti procur na neti ca'.

statements.claim: Their attention was wholly on the sacrifice — place, time, materials, mantras, rituals, priests, fires.
statements.evidence: SB 10.23.9: 'deśaḥ kālaḥ pṛthag dravyaṃ mantra-tantrartvijo 'gnayaḥ'.

statements.claim: They did not recognize the supreme Brahman, the Lord, who stood before them, hidden by their own learning.
statements.evidence: SB 10.23.10: 'taṃ brahma paramaṃ sākṣād bhagavantam adhokṣajam' — the supreme Brahman, directly the Lord Adhokṣaja; pack excerpt: 'proud of their learning, do not recognize the Lord'.

notes: Refusal episode matches SB 10.23.1-11 exactly, including the 'neither yes nor no' detail.

statements.claim: When Krishna heard what had happened, the master of the whole world laughed, without anger.
statements.evidence: SB 10.23.12: 'tad upākarṇya bhagavān prahasya jagad-īśvaraḥ' — hearing this, the Lord, master of the world, laughed.

statements.claim: He said: go to their wives, and tell them that I have come, with Balarama.
statements.evidence: SB 10.23.13: 'māṃ jñāpayata patnībhyaḥ sa-saṅkarṣaṇam āgatam' — announce to the wives that I have come with Saṅkarṣaṇa.

statements.claim: The boys bowed to the wives and said: "Obeisance to you, wives of the brahmanas; listen to our words. While pasturing the cows with the cowherds, he has come from far away, with Balarama — and he is hungry."
statements.evidence: SB 10.23.14-16: 'namo vo vipra-patnībhyo nibodhata vacāṃsi naḥ / gāś cārayan sa gopālaiḥ sa-rāmo dūram āgataḥ'; hunger from 10.23.6.

statements.claim: The wives, who had always longed for Krishna's sight, heard that Acyuta had come and rose at once.
statements.evidence: SB 10.23.17: 'śrutvācyutam upāyātaṃ nityaṃ tad-darśanotsukāḥ' — hearing Acyuta had come, they who were always longing for his sight.

statements.claim: They filled vessels with food of four kinds, rich and fine, and hurried toward him.
statements.evidence: SB 10.23.18: 'catur-vidhaṃ bahu-guṇam annam ādāya bhājanaiḥ' — taking four kinds of excellent food in vessels.

statements.claim: Their husbands, brothers, kinsmen and sons tried to stop them.
statements.evidence: SB 10.23.19: 'niṣidhyamānāḥ patibhir bhrātṛbhir bandhubhiḥ sutaiḥ'.

statements.claim: Not one of them turned back; they went like rivers running to the sea.
statements.evidence: Pack excerpt: 'hurry to him like rivers to the sea, heedless of husbands and kinsmen who would stop them' (rendered from 10.23.12-19).

statements.claim: They left houses, husbands and kin without a backward look, running toward him as toward a light.
statements.evidence: Devotional framing of the 'heedless of husbands and kinsmen' detail (10.23.19); the 'light/arrival' imagery is narrative commentary, not a factual claim.

notes: Wives episode matches SB 10.23.12-19; no unsupported or contradicted claims.
